newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain sees UN approval for Zaire force in days.
newsitem.headline: Spain sees UN approval for Zaire force in days.

text.p: Spain was optimistic on Tuesday the United Nations would authorise deployment of a multinational force by Thursday to aid more than a million sick and starving refugees.
In eastern Zaire, the urgent need for intervention was underlined by a doctor's warning that an outbreak of cholera could wipe out some 250,000 refugees within days.

"I, who am reluctant to shout it from the rooftops, believe it is possible between today and tomorrow the Security Council will meet to approve the creation of a force," Spanish Foreign Minister Abel Matutes told reporters.
Senior U.N. officials said on Tuesday a huge airlift of supplies for Rwandan Hutu refugees fleeing Tutsi rebels in east Zaire may start before the end of the week.
Canada said it was ready to command a multinational force in Zaire to protect the relief operation and U.N. officials said the force could be on the ground as early as this weekend.
Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar called Canadian Premier Jean Chretien to stress the need for urgent opening of humanitarian corridors to facilitate distribution of aid.
He expressed his concern about deterioration of the situation in the war zone and lamented the delay in international decisions on intervention.

A U.N. doctor in Zaire said on Tuesday cholera had broken out at a hillside settlement of about 250,000 Rwanda Hutu refugees outside the town of Bukavu and could wipe out its entire population within days.

In Madrid, thousands of demonstrators filled Plaza Mayor, the city's central square, in solidarity with the victims of war in Zaire. The demonstrators, among them many nuns and priests, demanded urgent government action and criticised the United Nations for being slow to act.
Similar vigils were held in other major cities across Spain.

Spanish parliament passed a resolution demanding a "limited military action" under a U.N. mandate in Zaire. It called on the European Union to adopt common initiatives to promote peace and human rights in the area.
The U.N. Security Council on Saturday asked members to lay the groundwork for a multinational force but held off authorising it until its aims and participation were clearer.
"Today Canada, like Italy, Belgium and Holland are in favour of this force being put together and Britain and the United States are also considering this possibility," Matutes said.
"Before they were talking about logistical supprt and (now) they are even talking about placing personnel on the ground."
France, spearheading with Spain the efforts to deploy a multinational force, stepped up criticism of the United States on Tuesday and said Washington was dragging its feet.

The United States is edging towards involvement but has sought additional information on the role of the force, command lines and an "exit scenario" while pursuing political solutions to pacify eastern Zaire.
Spain has put troops on alert for an immediate action, should the U.N. give a green light.
Matutes said on Tuesday 350 to 450 Spanish troops would participate initially in the force -- up to 50 percent more than mentioned before. Spain may later increase the numbers.
